bug_semantics: ChaiScript accepted recursively re-entering user-defined script functions without any maximum call-depth check. The disclosed script defines string::`/=` so its body evaluates `${this/= 2}`, immediately dispatching the same operator again; eval_function and AST_Node_Impl::eval repeatedly enter Function_Push_Pop/new_function_call until the native thread stack is exhausted and the host aborts with stack-overflow/SIGSEGV. An attacker needs a local path to make the host evaluate supplied ChaiScript, and the resulting impact is denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 first made script-defined functions executable: it added eval_function0 through eval_function3 in wesley/main.cpp, each directly returning eval_token(ss, node), and changed Function_Def evaluation from a no-op into registration of those callbacks, with no recursion bound. Later header moves, AST rewrites, Stack_Holder/call_depth bookkeeping, operator support, and string interpolation only preserved or exposed that already-unbounded script-function re-entry; they are not the first causal commit.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140` records author and committer Jonathan Turner <probata@hotmail.com>, timestamp 2009-06-04, and only the subject `Trying to add function definitions, but not quite there`; it has no body, trailer, Co-Authored-By/Generated-with marker, AI identity, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/issues/633 supplies the recursive string::`/=` PoC and ASAN trace through Equation_AST_Node::eval_internal, AST_Node_Impl::eval, Function_Push_Pop, and eval_function to native stack exhaustion. In the validated clone, `git log --reverse -L 94,118:wesley/main.cpp 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140` shows 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 adding all four eval_function callbacks and their unguarded `return eval_token(ss, node)` calls; `git log --all --reverse -S'return eval_token(ss, node);' -- wesley/main.cpp wesley/wesley_eval.hpp chaiscript/chaiscript_eval.hpp include/chaiscript/language/chaiscript_eval.hpp` independently returns that commit first. `git show 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140` also shows Function_Def becoming active callback registration. Direct parent verification: `git grep -n -E 'eval_function[0-9]|register_function.*node->children' 53301ccb66bf9ca30805fc9cc41dc2a544467d69 -- wesley/main.cpp` has no match, while `git show 53301ccb66bf9ca30805fc9cc41dc2a544467d69:wesley/main.cpp` shows TokenType::Function_Def grouped with ignored token types. The one-parent BIC commit object names that parent, so no squash decomposition is involved. Release boundary: `git for-each-ref --contains=8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 --sort=creatordate refs/tags` begins with v1.0.0/Release-1.0.0 at 599a21d377073027d7ea7ac9b44df28c34f19cf9; `git show v1.0.0:include/chaiscript/language/chaiscript_eval.hpp` contains unbounded eval_function recursion. `git show v6.1.0:include/chaiscript/dispatchkit/dispatchkit.hpp` shows new_function_call incrementing call_depth without a bound, matching the advisory's affected-through-6.1.0 statement. `git show 85b8e7c0c84f53c4a2467c51d8d9a3bfd7f4f90f` shows the direct closing patch: check `t_s.call_depth >= max_call_depth` before increment, throw stack_overflow_error, define platform-sensitive defaults (256; 32 for MSVC Debug), and add the issue PoC regression. `git tag --contains 85b8e7c0c84f53c4a2467c51d8d9a3bfd7f4f90f` returns no tags, so the fix landed on develop on 2026-05-02 but had no tagged fixed release in this history.
reasoning: The causal defect is not the reporter's particular operator spelling or string interpolation alone; it is the engine's ability to re-enter script-defined function bodies indefinitely without bounding native recursion. Commit 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140 is the smallest first-writer because it activates user-defined function callbacks whose bodies recursively call eval_token, and its direct parent treats Function_Def as a no-op. Git -L and -S agree, while later file moves and evaluator refactors merely carry the same behavior forward. Commit 85b8e7c0c84f53c4a2467c51d8d9a3bfd7f4f90f closes the mechanism at the shared dispatcher frame entry, before native stack exhaustion, and is itself the atomic landed fix. Although that later fix commit contains Claude Opus co-author trailers, the protocol permits AI judgment only from the BIC commit object. The 2009 BIC has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the vulnerability is NOT_AI.
